summary: Sound, rules-clean, readable from top_kernels (the memset row vanishes and _router_hilo_sem_kernel's own time shows the tail cost), but it sits on master's small-m router config that the two running splitk32 runs may replace. Defer dispatch until router-splitk32-small-m-all-loads-in-flight and its stages3 control harvest, then build it on whichever small-m config wins, with SPLIT_K as a constexpr instead of a hardcoded 16.
justification: The mechanism holds up. FINDINGS shows the router m<=32 rows as _router_hilo_kernel 3.3-4.1 us plus at::native::vectorized_elementwise_kernel (the torch.zeros fill) 0.7-0.8 us in its own graph node, with 5.7-6.5 us reported. LESSONS puts a single Triton graph node at ~0.3 us of reported-minus-kernel, so removing the memset node can save at most ~0.8 + 0.3 = ~1.1 us per row, about 15-19% of the router row at m=1/8/16. The floor is 1.8-1.9 us, so there is room. The headline effect is small: four of 30 shapes at -10..-18% is about +1.2-2% on the geomean, near LESSONS' ~1.5% single-run limit. Judge it per shape; Triton rows reproduce within ~1%. The expected directions agree with TASK: m=1/8/16/32 take the changed buckets, and m=128/256 (verify_16/32) are untouched in-run controls. WEAKEST LINK: the hypothesis prices the new epilogue only by bytes. It ignores the serial latency added to the last-arriving CTA of each N-tile, which is the critical path. Master's relaxed fp32 atomic_add is fire-and-forget reds. The new tail is a dependent chain: partial store, then bar.sync, then a gpu-scope acq_rel atomic round trip to L2 (~0.5-1 us), then 16 .cg L2 loads (one more round trip if they are issued together, 16 if they are emitted as a dependent loop), then the final store and the xchg. That can be ~1-1.5 us, roughly the size of the saving, so 'faster' at m=1/8/16 is a toss-up, not a given, and decode_32's 'flat' could just as well be 'slower'. Implementation must-dos: load all 16 partials before the first add (tl.static_range so the loads are hoisted, or one [SPLIT_K, BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N] tile load), then add in fixed order 0..SPLIT_K-1. Make the partial store and reload use the same masked [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N] footprint, so rows >= m in the workspace are never read unmasked. The ticket/barrier/xchg pattern itself is proven by the pooler and qkv-gate semaphore checks (LESSONS, DECISIONS 2026-10-24T090934Z).
confounders: router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m (landed, master's router): this hypothesis edits that kernel's epilogue directly. The tail cost scales with its SPLIT_K (16 partials) and its grid (8 N-tiles x 16 = 128 CTAs, one wave), so a gain or loss is specific to master's (16|32, 32, 16) small-m buckets. That is intended and attributable as long as the base stays the same.

router-splitk32-small-m-all-loads-in-flight and its stages3 control (running, not landed, but they would land on exactly these buckets): SPLIT_K=32 doubles the number of partials the winner reloads (32 x 4 KB = 128 KB at m=32) and grows the workspace to (32, 32, 256). It also doubles the atomics this change removes, and at 256 CTAs it can change which CTA finishes last. The semaphore's value therefore differs between SPLIT_K=16 and 32 in both directions: more is saved (no doubled atomics, same memset) and the tail is longer. A SPLIT_K=16 result does not carry over to a SPLIT_K=32 master.

sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity and router-hilo-at-m8: no confound. The router path they changed is gone from master (replaced wholesale by the split-K Triton kernel), and the bf16 layers' dispatch does not touch the router's launch sequence or memory.
interference: No companion is needed for the run itself. The profile already separates the two sub-effects: the memset kernel either disappears from top_kernels or it does not, and the new kernel's own time versus master's 3.3-4.1 us gives the tail cost directly. A gain or a loss is interpretable without an A/B, and the verify_16/32 rows are in-run controls. The real interference is sequencing against the splitk32 pair already in the judge. Its harvest is imminent and it changes the exact buckets this kernel replaces. If this is dispatched now at SPLIT_K=16 and splitk32 then gains, the result is stale. It would measure an epilogue on a config master has abandoned, it cannot be combined without a re-run (the hypothesis says so itself), and rebuilding it on the new master would silently revert the splitk32 gain. Recommendation: wait for that harvest, which costs one tick and no quota. If splitk32 (num_stages=2) or its stages3 control is a gain, write this on the winning config: SPLIT_K=32, the winning num_stages, workspace (32, 32, 256), winner on ticket == SPLIT_K-1. In that case decode_32 should be expected flat-to-slower because of the 128 KB serial reload. If both are neutral or regress, run it as written at SPLIT_K=16. Either way, write SPLIT_K as a constexpr (ticket == SPLIT_K-1, workspace sized from _router_config) so the choice is one line.
rules_flags: None blocking. state['router_ws'] and state['router_cnt'] are allocated in prepare(), are not derived from data, and are fully overwritten or reset every call: control and scratch state, not a cache of inputs.

The counter must read zero at every graph capture and after every replay. The winner's atomic_xchg reset plus re-zeroing after prepare()'s warm-up covers this, because the judge runs graphs in turns, not concurrently. All router shapes share the one counter and workspace, which is safe only under that serial replay; note it in a comment.

No host syncs, and no branching on values (the ticket branch is device-side). The output stays fp32 with fp32 accumulation of hi+lo, within the TASK allowance. The fixed-order sum makes the router deterministic, which helps the 0.01% / 0.1% single-nonzero-row bounds.
open_questions: Which small-m config wins in the splitk32 pair (num_stages=2 vs 3, or neither)? That decides SPLIT_K=16 or 32 for this build.
Does Triton emit the scalar acq_rel ticket by one thread with a broadcast (an extra smem barrier on the winner path)? Check the TTGIR/PTX in the implement step; it adds to the tail.

If the tail eats the saving, the cheaper follow-up is to keep the relaxed atomics and remove only the memset by having split 0 zero-and-add under a ticket. That still needs ordering, so it is probably no better. Worth a line in FINDINGS whichever way this lands.
